title: Palantir Foundry and federal data-sharing concerns
description_medium: A May 30, 2025 report in The New York Times, summarized in the supplied packet by NBC News and The New Republic, described Palantir’s Foundry software in use at several federal agencies and discussions about expanding access. Foundry can organize and analyze records held by separate agencies, raising concerns about how linked data might be used.
description_long: The May 30, 2025 account concerned federal use of Palantir Technologies’ Foundry software and efforts to make agency records easier to analyze together. The New York Times report, as summarized in the supplied material by NBC News and The New Republic, said Foundry was in use at at least four agencies, including Homeland Security and Health and Human Services, and was under discussion with the Social Security Administration and the IRS. The reporting described efforts to access records involving finances, medical claims, student debt and disability, alongside data requests associated with DOGE. Some access efforts faced court blocks while others continued. Palantir said client agencies control their accounts and permitted uses. Privacy advocates warned that combining records could expand government surveillance. These reports document software use, data requests and concerns about potential scope. They do not establish that the government assembled a profile of every American, or that information was used to blackmail critics or elected officials. Those stronger claims would require evidence about actual datasets, access and use.

title: Trump removes Nuclear Regulatory Commission member Christopher Hanson

description_long: On June 16, 2025, President Donald Trump removed Christopher Hanson from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, where Hanson had been serving as chairman.
